instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.62(10) defines "lobbying" as attempting to influence legislative/administrative action by oral or written communication, including time spent in preparation and appearances at public hearings, meetings, or service on a committee.
Section 13.62(11) defines "lobbyist" as an individual employed by a principal, or who contracts for or receives economic consideration from a principal, whose duties include lobbying.

Section 13.62(2) defines "agency" as any board, commission, department, office, society, institution of higher education, council, or committee in state government, or specified authorities — a definition of a public/state entity.

The statute includes materiality thresholds: §13.62(11) requires lobbying communications on at least 5 days per reporting period for mixed-duty individuals, and §13.64(1) triggers principal registration only when expenditures exceed $500 in a calendar year.

Lobbying under §13.62(10) includes attempting to influence "administrative action" (defined in §13.62(1) as rulemaking by any agency) by communication with agency officials, so executive agencies are covered targets.

Section 13.62(3) defines "agency official" to include members, officers, employees, or consultants of an agency, and §13.62(10) includes communications with agency officials as lobbying, covering executive branch staff.

The Governor is a "partisan elective state official" under §13.62(11p) and an "elective state official" under §13.62(6); §13.62(8) explicitly includes the Governor's action in approving/vetoing bills and developing proposals as "legislative action," making the Governor's office a lobbying target.

Section 13.62(2)'s definition of "agency" expressly includes authorities created in subch. II of ch. 114 or chs. 231, 232, 233, 234, 237, 238, or 279 — i.e., independent authorities — bringing them within the lobbying targets.

Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying as attempting to influence legislative action through communication with elective state officials or legislative employees; §13.62(8) defines "legislative action" as actions by the legislature, its houses, committees, or legislators.

Section 13.62(8m) defines "legislative employee" to include members/officers of the legislature, individuals employed under §13.20, and legislative service agency employees, and §13.62(10) treats communications with legislative employees as lobbying.

Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying as communication with "elective state official," which §13.62(6) defines as a person holding elective state office — confirming elected officials are a covered target class.

Section 13.62(10) includes communications with agency officials and legislative employees; §13.62(3) defines agency officials to include employees and §13.62(8m) defines legislative employees, confirming public employees are targets.

Section 13.62(2) identifies covered agencies by their creation/charter under specific statutory chapters (subch. II of ch. 114, chs. 231, 232, 233, 234, 237, 238, 279), relying on the entity's statutory charter/creation.

Section 13.62(2)'s definition of agency turns on the entity being a state government body or authority created under designated chapters; it does not reference government ownership as a definitional criterion.
Section 13.62(2) defines agency by its institutional nature and statutory creation, with no reference to funding source, revenue structure, or appropriations as a criterion.
